population: Finnish men: Helsinki Birth Cohort Study (43 healthy longer-living men vs 92 men who died of natural causes at mean age 66.6) plus a replication group of 63 healthy men (mean age 83) from the Helsinki Businessmen Study
conclusion: T allele heterozygotes: 1/43 healthy longer-living vs 9/92 early-deceased controls (HBCS), 2/63 in the HBS replication group. Combined longer-living vs controls: OR 3.58 (95% CI 0.96-13.4), p = 0.074 (Table 2; the abstract prints OR 3.53). A trend toward the T allele in men who died earlier, not significant; stated power 28.4%. No T/T homozygotes observed. The paper classes the variant as intronic, 23 bases downstream of the exon 2/intron border (the ClinGen Allele Registry names it NM_016539.4:c.194+194G>A, also intronic).
study_design: case-control, direct PCR sequencing of SIRT6 exons
statistical_test: two-tailed Fisher's exact test (PLINK), HBCS and HBS longer-living men combined vs HBCS controls
provenance_quote: These study findings suggest an inverse association between the T allele of rs117385980 and longevity in Finnish men.
effect_unit: prevalence odds ratio for the T allele, early-deceased controls vs longer-living healthy men (95% CI 0.96-13.4)

population: Older adults aged 60-90 from the Birjand Longitudinal Aging Study, Birjand, Iran: 227 randomly sampled participants (39 frail, 150 pre-frail, 38 robust; 121 women, 106 men)
conclusion: T allele frequency by age group: 1.39% at 60-69, 4.65% at 70-79, 0% at 80-90 (4/144, 4/43 and 0/40 heterozygotes; p = 0.073, Table 4). Not a steady decline (60-69 vs 80-90 p = 0.37), cross-sectional, no mortality data. The study's primary outcome, Fried frailty, showed no association (final adjusted model OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.10-9.66, p = 0.98). No T/T homozygotes observed. The paper calls the variant stop-gained in exon 2, which disagrees with its own cited source (intronic) and with the ClinGen Allele Registry (CA15948970, NM_016539.4:c.194+194G>A, intronic); see README.
study_design: case-control within a community cohort, PCR-RFLP genotyping with Sanger confirmation of 3 samples
statistical_test: Fisher's exact test, allelic, T allele frequency across three age groups (60-69, 70-79, 80-90 years)
provenance_quote: the frequency of the T allele was numerically lower in the 80–90 years age group (0%) compared to the 60–69 (1.39%) and 70–79 (4.65%) age groups
